summary: Forest Service lookout on Nason Ridge, Chelan County. A 1936 L-4 cab was replaced by an R-6 cab in 1975; a 2019 plan says the 1936 building still stands.

facts.design: R-6 flat-top cab (1975), replacing a 1936 L-4 cab

access.note: Reached on foot by trail. The register says the cab remains in active service; the sources read do not say whether visitors may enter it.

visit.trail_note: About 10 miles round trip with about 2,600 ft of gain, from a trailhead reached by FR 6910 off US 2. NW Forest Pass or interagency pass required (2025 hiking guide).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The sources date different stages: 1920 is the first fire-watch camp, 1936 the first L-4 cab, and 1975 the R-6 cab standing now. The record's 1936 refers to the first cab, not the current structure. Whether the 1936 building still stands is not resolved.

sources.title: Nason Ridge Community Forest Management Plan (2019)

notes_for_editor: The 1936 building question is unresolved: a 2019 plan citing a 2009 USFS source says it still stands, while the register and firelookout.com say the L-4 was replaced in 1975. Staffing rests on one 2025 hiking guide and an undated register entry. Unread search snippets, not used in the story: SummitPost and an Alamy caption give 1976 for the R-6 cab; a hiking site mentions a 1924 occupant and 1935 radio; Trailchick says staffing was seasonal in the past. The record's 1936 built event is the first L-4 cab, not the cab standing today. Page reads for this lookout: four.
